items.rationale: Sections 5.2.6 and 5.2.7 cover necessary dismantling and refitting for access or drying, but not repair of the failed seal itself absent an insured fracture. Case 46 supports €90 for the separate access service.

Section 5.2.7 covers necessary drying supported by moisture readings. The seven billed days fall within the reported drying period and are estimated at €313 gross, with no addition for the unbilled days.
Section 7.4.4 bars an unitemised material surcharge. The €39 estimate applies only if an itemised breakdown establishes that the materials were necessary and not already included elsewhere.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(c) allow like-for-like mineral-wool insulation if it was damaged or necessarily removed for access. One unit is estimated at €26 gross.
Section 5.2.2 allows disposal of the actual insured debris once and gives priority to the first charge. The first-listed disposal charge is estimated at €60 gross for the small load.
Section 5.2.6 covers levelling needed to make good the affected basement wall. The comparable material line supports €38 gross.

Section 5.2.6 covers necessary preparation of the damaged wall, but sections 3.5(d) and 7.4.1 bar overlap with the separate levelling and labour charges. If this is distinct preparation, 2.78 m² at about €29/m² gives €81 gross.
Section 5.2.6 expressly covers a necessary service opening, provided its labour is not already charged elsewhere. Case 46 supports about €19 gross for one opening.

The tiles are at the inclusive limit in section 7.14(d), but sections 3.5(a) and 7.1.5 still require comparable grade and a justified quantity, including cuts. At about €42/m² for standard-grade tile, five pieces covering 4.05 m² give €170 gross.

The tiles exceed the 90 × 90 cm limit in section 7.14(d), and section 3.5(f) bars partial payment on a line that exceeds the standard threshold. The €170 conditional figure reflects a standard-grade equivalent for the damaged area, not the designer order.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(a) allow standard sanitary silicone joints in the reinstated area. At about €13 per metre, 3.6 m gives €47 gross.
Section 7.4.2 allows the first necessary travel charge per contractor per document. The single tiling travel charge is estimated at €81 gross.
Section 7.4.1 allows customary labour for necessary basement work, excluding hours included in other lines or spent on the attic. For 14 qualifying hours, the supplied prior gives €1,239 gross.

items.description: Remove basement drywall and insulation wool
items.rationale: Sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.6 cover necessary removal in the affected basement, subject to adequate breakdown under section 7.4.4 and no duplicate disposal. Case 46 supports about €50 for drywall and €40 for insulation removal, or €90 gross.
Section 5.2.6 covers necessary removal of damp plaster in the documented basement damage area. The supplied prior assigns €29 gross to the one billed unit.
Sections 3.5(b) and 7.1.5 exclude the unrelated attic work because no leak damage was established there. The €29 conditional figure uses the comparable single-unit plaster removal rate.
Sections 3.5(d) and 5.2.2 exclude this second charge for the same disposal, even though a different contractor billed it. The €60 conditional figure is the benchmark for one eligible disposal charge.
